proton-transfer.alt: An HF molecule passes an H⁺ (curved arrow) to a water molecule. HF is the acid, the proton donor; water is the base, the proton acceptor. The products are F⁻, the conjugate base, and H₃O⁺, the conjugate acid. Brackets join HF with F⁻ and H₂O with H₃O⁺ as conjugate pairs, each differing by one H⁺. Equation: HF(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ F⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq).
